title: Multi-omics analysis elucidates the impacts of anthocyanins from various fruit pulps on bacterial communities, metabolites and proteins in yogurt.
byline: Liu M, Pan Y, Tong J, et al.
html: Fruit pulp fortification improves the nutritional profile and bioactive functionality of yogurt. In this study, we adopted 16S rRNA gene sequencing, UHPLC-MS-based metabolomics and DIA (data-independent acquisition)-based proteomics on raw milk, plain yogurt and five different anthocyanin-rich fruit yogurts. The work intended to clarify how anthocyanins in fruit pulp reshape yogurt composition and identify signature microbes and substances to each group. Besides Streptococcus, the dominant genera in plain, mulberry and grape yogurt were respectively Lactococcus, Lacticaseibacillus/Lactobacillus, and Bifidobacterium. β-D-fucose accumulated abundantly in plain yogurt. Abscisic acid exhibited higher levels in strawberry yogurt. It was positively correlated to Lactobacillus acidophilus and L. delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus. Furthermore, it downregulated α S1 -casein, a major milk allergen. Grape yogurt contained elevated levels of astilbin, eriocitrin and glucosylxanthone. In conclusion, yogurt microbiota, metabolites and proteins could be modified by fruit anthocyanins. Our findings advance a deeper understanding on the unique health-promoting effects of various fruit yogurt.
